newsitem.title: INDIA: India undecided on VSNL -BT venture.
newsitem.headline: India undecided on VSNL -BT venture.

text.p: India has yet to decide on a proposed 16 billion rupee ($447.3 million) joint venture between state-owned Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) and British Telecommunications plc (BT), a senior official said on Monday.

"The proposal has neither been accepted nor rejected. There are several matters of policy involved, and we cannot take a hasty decision on it," A V Gokak, chairman of the Telecom Commission, told a news conference.

Besides heading the Commission, Gokak is the senior-most official in Department of Telecommunications, which has enjoyed decades of monopoly in telephone services. India ended the monopoly in 1991, under an economic reform programme.
The VSNL-BT joint venture calls for the setting up of a hub for international traffic of data, images and sound, as well as the laying of submarine cables to carry the traffic.
Under the proposal, all international traffic between Britain and the Middle East, South Asia and South East Asia would be grouped in India and then transmitted to Britain.
Two policy issues are holding up the decision, Gokak said.
"We do not know whether the hubbing of traffic in India would mean the negation of VSNL's monopoly for international traffic (from India)," Gokak said.

"And we do not know whether the nation-wide backbone (of telecommunications infrastructure) which has been proposed in the venture would mean the negation of DoT's monopoly on national long-distance services," Gokak added.

DoT's monopoly on national long distance will be reviewed in 1999, while VSNL's monopoly on international traffic will end in 2004 under a global accord in telecommunications supervised by the World Trade Organisation (WTO). ($1=35.77 rupees)
